invariant-active-empty-not-partial-found: The Rust run-loop 'active stash exhausted' termination path (run_loop_parallel_wave / run_loop_parallel_steady / run_loop_single_threaded in exploration/run_loop.rs) MUST return ExplorationEvent::active_empty, NOT found, even when found_count()>0. That path is only reachable with found_count()<num_find because the top-of-loop path (a) returns 'found' for >=num_find before draining active. The Python _explore_with_addresses loop breaks on a 'found' event only when found_count>=num_find; a partial-count 'found' with an empty active stash is neither a break nor active_empty, so run() is re-invoked forever (unbounded spin, looks like a hang at 100% single-core CPU inside the Python loop, not the scheduler). This was angr-q1mwl (test_parallel_wave.py hang). Latent in single-threaded too: explore(find=X, num_find > reachable-finds) would hang identically. Returning active_empty lets the angr-027h phase-2 eager retry fire.

invariant-address-containment-wrapping-d:
Overflow triage: the single most common address-arith bug shape in this codebase is the two-comparison containment test `addr >= base && addr < base + size` (and its range variant `min < base + size`). `base + size` overflows for a region abutting the top of the guest address space, so the shipped .so wraps it to a small value and the test reports every in-region address as OUTSIDE — a silent wrong answer, not a crash. Rewrite as the single wrapping-distance comparison `addr.wrapping_sub(base) < size`: same result for a non-wrapping region, correct for a wrapping one, and it never forms base+size. Canonical implementation: `ConcreteMemoryRegion::offset_of`/`contains` (interpreter/concrete_memory.rs) and `covering_range` (interpreter/pending_store.rs), which does the same for a load range and hands back the slice `Range<usize>` so the `off + size` index sum is proven in-bounds by construction rather than re-checked at each call site. Where the test is a range-vs-range intersection and a conservative over-estimate is safe, `saturating_add` plus an `overflow-ok:` comment naming that fact is fine (statements_store.rs::invalidate_code_for_concretization's TooLarge arm). Found in angr-xloth.3; expect the same shape repeatedly in the remaining memory/ triage.

COROLLARY (angr-fs8kb.63, PendingStoreBuffer::push): the 'saturating_add is fine for a range-vs-range intersection' escape hatch above is only safe when you check WHICH DIRECTION the error goes. For a range that wraps past the top of the address space, saturating_add clamps the end to u64::MAX and therefore UNDER-estimates the covered set — it silently drops the wrapped tail (addresses 0..). So it is conservative only for a consumer where a missed overlap is the safe answer (invalidate_code_for_concretization over-invalidates, so it is). push's overlap-patch loop was the opposite: a missed overlap means an earlier store's buffer is never patched, and try_load's reverse-scan fallback later serves the stale pre-overwrite byte. Rule: compute a range intersection in OFFSET space, never in address space — derive both offsets with wrapping_sub from one of the two bases and take the min of the remaining lengths, the way overlap_offsets (interpreter/pending_store.rs) does beside covering_range. Neither end address is ever formed, so there is nothing to saturate or wrap.

COROLLARY 2 (angr-fs8kb.64): the same gap existed on the SYMBOLIC-store side — symbolic_overlap_load (interpreter/expressions.rs) and evict_overlapping_symbolic_stores (interpreter/statements_store.rs) each re-derived the interval arithmetic in address space. Both now call the pending_store.rs helpers, which are `pub(super)` precisely so the interpreter has exactly ONE wraparound-safe coverage test (covering_range) and ONE overlap test (overlap_offsets). If you find a fourth site asking either question, reuse them rather than writing a local wrapping_sub — three independent re-derivations is how this family kept recurring, and only the shared helper carries the doc explaining why no end address may be formed.
invariant-address-newtype-ops-already-wr: memory/ overflow triage: the `Address` newtype (native/angr/src/memory/address.rs) implements Add<u64>/Sub<u64>/Sub<Address> as wrapping_*, so an `addr + i`/`addr - base` site whose operand is an Address is ALREADY in the sanctioned state (address arithmetic wraps — invariant-rust-concrete-arith-must-wrap) and needs no wrapping_* rewrite. tools/audit_overflow_wraparound.py is a textual scan and cannot see the type, so it reports every one of them; that is the dominant false-positive class in the memory/ baseline (roughly 30 of the 69 sites triaged under angr-xloth.4). Do NOT 'fix' them by adding .wrapping_add on the raw() value — that loses the newtype. Mark them with a short `overflow-ok: Address ops are wrapping_*` comment, and note the exception that matters: wrapping makes the op non-panicking, NOT semantically correct. A wrapped sum used in a COMPARISON is still a bug — containing_wider_sym's `addr + size <= base_addr + sym_size` was wrapping and still wrong (see invariant-address-containment-wrapping-distance; the memory/ canonical fix is now Address::offset_in / Address::range_in). INVERSE BLIND SPOT (angr-fs8kb.69): the audit's false-NEGATIVE class is the mirror image — a site that ESCAPES the newtype to hand-roll saturating/checked arith on .raw(), e.g. `Address(current.raw().saturating_add(n))` in SymbolicMemory::read_concrete_bytes_for_lift. The scan matches bare +/- operators only, so a method call is invisible to it *and* silently opts that one site out of the file's wrapping convention. For an address cursor, saturating is not a safe conservative choice: it clamps to u64::MAX and the enclosing loop then re-visits the same last byte/page instead of wrapping to page 0 (that read returned a duplicated trailing byte to the lifter). When triaging a file for this class, grep `.raw()` for saturating_/checked_/wrapping_ alongside running the audit — and when writing a top-of-address-space regression, always assert the whole returned buffer, not just its length, since the corruption is in the contents.
invariant-address-vs-page-number: When carving a newtype out of u64 for a subsystem, distinguish byte ADDRESSES from PAGE NUMBERS (addr >> 12). Two complementary newtypes now exist: memory::Address wraps byte addresses (see native/angr/src/memory/address.rs for the documented migration pattern), and memory::PageIndex (memory/page.rs, angr-91vj9.8) wraps page numbers for callers ABOVE the memory layer — VEXInterpreter::dirtied_code_pages, syscalls/mmap.rs::range_collides, syscalls/mprotect.rs::NativeMprotectSyscall::call. Its PageIndex::range_covering(addr, len) replaces the open-coded 'first..=last' page loops (it is empty for len==0 and saturates instead of wrapping). INVARIANT (angr-fs8kb.49): a page walk must iterate page NUMBERS via range_covering, never step a byte address by PAGE_SIZE ('while a < end { ...; a += PAGE_SIZE }'). That shape is structurally broken at the top of the address space — an end computed as '(last_byte & !PAGE_MASK).saturating_add(PAGE_SIZE)' saturates to the non-page-aligned u64::MAX, so a page-aligned start can never reach it and ALWAYS overflows on the step after the final page: silent wrap to 0 in [profile.release] (walk resumes from low memory → false -1 or ~2^52-iteration hang), panic under release-checked. tools/audit_overflow_wraparound.py cannot see it — BINOP_RE's (?![=>]) lookahead excludes compound assignment (tracked as angr-fs8kb.52). Page numbers are under 2^52, so range_covering has no per-iteration overflow to get wrong. Matching rule for the range guard: only the LAST BYTE must be representable (addr.checked_add(length - 1)), so a region ending exactly at 2^64 is legal — do_mmap's MAP_FIXED guard and mprotect now agree on this. The page-keyed structures INSIDE memory/ (pages: OrdMap<u64, MemoryPage>, dirty_pages: FxHashSet<u64>, lazy_regions: Vec<(u64,u64)>) and the raw page API they expose (page_permissions) deliberately stay raw u64 — callers cross that boundary explicitly with PageIndex::get()/from_raw(). MemoryError variants also keep u64 to preserve existing Display formatting. Address-keyed structures in memory/: symbolic_objects, symbolic_spans, multi_objects, multi_versions, imported_addrs, wider_load_cache.
invariant-arc-make-mut-cow: Pattern for read-mostly fields in RustSimState that need O(1) fork: wrap in Arc<T> and use Arc::make_mut on mutation. For methods that mutate, peek the read path first to skip the CoW clone when the operation would be a no-op (e.g. fd not found, nothing to read, invalid arg, re-adding an element already present, setting a key to the value it already holds). Otherwise every call to the mutator forces a deep clone even when no real change happens. See FileSystem::close/read/seek, RustSimState::clear_hooks/add_hook/remove_hook/set_option/setenv/unsetenv for the pattern. PER-ARC, NOT PER-METHOD: a mutator that unconditionally mutates one Arc field still needs the peek on every OTHER Arc it touches — FileSystem::install_fd always inserts into fds, but known_paths is a separate Arc, so re-opening an already-known path was deep-cloning that set for nothing (angr-5mnx3.38, fixed by the shared FileSystem::note_known_path peek helper). Do not reason 'this call always mutates, so the peek is pointless'. Avoid Arc-wrap for fields mutated on every fork (e.g. RegisterFile.symbolic) — make_mut churn would offset the savings. SAME RULE for im::OrdMap fields (SymbolicMemory::pages): OrdMap::get_mut copies the tree path down to the target key even if the closure changes nothing, so probe with the read-only get() before taking &mut — see SymbolicMemory::clear_multi_at (angr-fgqco), whose no-op path runs once per byte of every symbolic store. TESTING THIS INVARIANT: asserting on the collection's CONTENTS after a no-op mutation passes whether or not the clone was skipped, so it proves nothing — that vacuity is how five mutators drifted off the invariant unnoticed (angr-0jh0j.47). The only observable that distinguishes 'skipped the clone' from 'cloned into an equal value' is Arc::ptr_eq against a fork taken before the mutation; see state/tests/cow_peek.rs::shares_after and state/filesystem/tests.rs's *_skips_cow_clone tests.
invariant-arc-shared-soundness: The clippy::arc_with_non_send_sync suppression in arc_shared (native/angr/src/lib.rs) is NOT justified by single-threadedness — the engine steps states on real OS worker threads (exploration::scheduler_pool::worker_thread, named angr-worker-N). It is sound because RustSimState/SymContext are !Send by design and the ONLY cross-thread transport is StateMigrationPayload (state/migration.rs), which is Send-by-construction and compile-time guarded by assert_send::<StateMigrationPayload>(); no unsafe impl Send/Sync exists in production code. So an arc_shared Arc cannot escape its worker except via detach_for_migration/reattach, which rebuilds the shared state on the destination thread. A contributor adding a genuinely cross-thread Arc must route it through that payload — do not widen the suppression. Same rationale now documented at SymContext::with_timeout (symbolic/context.rs) and SymContext::fork (symbolic/snapshot_fork_ops.rs). angr-e6p38, commit cac6f6a10.
invariant-arch-aliases-complete: arch_from_name (native/angr/src/arch/registry.rs) accepted names must all resolve to a CallingConvention. Since angr-9ke6b.216 both sides read ONE table: ALL_ARCHES (arch/registry.rs), a const slice of ArchDesc { name, aliases, vex, make_arch, make_cc }; arch_from_name/arch_from_vex/cc_for_arch/default_cc_for_arch all iterate it via arch_desc_from_name, so the completeness invariant is structural rather than a coincidence between two hand-written lists. To add an alias, add it to the ALL_ARCHES row.
invariant-arch-aliases-disjoint: ALL_ARCHES (native/angr/src/arch/registry.rs) name+aliases spellings must stay disjoint across rows. arch_desc_from_name walks the table in declaration order, so a spelling in two rows makes both arch_from_name and default_cc_for_arch silently order-dependent. test_arch_aliases_disjoint (arch/calling_conventions_tests.rs) pins this; do not weaken it. Decision recorded there: 'mips64be' is deliberately NOT a registered name — MIPS64 big-endian states are built as 'mips64' + Iend_BE; it used to sit in MipsN64::ARCH_ALIASES while arch_from_name rejected it, and the merge resolved that by rejecting it everywhere (test_mips64be_is_not_a_registered_arch_name).
invariant-arch-canonical-is-the-python-e:
arch/*.rs CANONICAL vs ALIASES is NOT a naming taxonomy — it is the gate on what crosses the Python boundary. Only CANONICAL entries feed REGISTER_NAMES, which drives BOTH directions: RustStateSyncMixin._supported_register_names on the way in and RustSimState::export_full's named_registers on the way out. A register parked in ALIASES is therefore silently unexported: a Python-set state.regs.<name> is dropped and a guest-computed value never comes back, each side reading 0 with no error. ARM's whole VFP file (d0-d31, fpscr, tpidruro, itstate) and AArch64's q0-q31/cc_*/tpidr_el0/qcflag/fpcr shipped this way for the life of the branch (angr-l8kfw).

Rules when adding/auditing an arch table:
1. Distinct guest storage with no other canonical entry covering the same bytes => CANONICAL. Only an overlapping SPELLING of storage some canonical entry already covers stays in ALIASES (x86 sub-registers, ARM32 qN over its dN pair, AArch64 vN/dN under qN). Exactly one spelling per offset may be canonical or Arch::register_name(offset) picks arbitrarily between them.
2. Prefer the FULL-WIDTH spelling as the canonical one (AArch64 qN, not dN) — a narrower canonical name truncates the register on export.
3. An exported name must also exist in archinfo's registers dict for that arch, or _sync_registers_to_rust's getattr(state.regs, name) raises. ARM32 has no qN in archinfo at all — that, not the overlap, is why qN cannot be exported there.
4. The VEX bookkeeping tail (emnote/cmstart/cmlen/nraddr/ip_at_syscall) stays alias-only on every arch; AMD64 is the reference for where the line sits.
arch::registry_tests::every_narrow_canonical_register_is_exported enforces rule 1's consequence but only over canonical_registers(), so it is blind to anything still in ALIASES — the gap has to be caught by reading the table.

TEST-DESIGN COROLLARY: a boundary round-trip test must assert on a register the GUEST computed, never on the one Python preset — the preset value is still in the Python state's own copy, so the assertion passes vacuously even with the channel fully broken. tests/engines/rust/test_multiarch.py::test_vector_registers_cross_the_python_boundary uses a guest vector move (vmov d0,d1 / mov v0.16b,v1.16b) so both halves must work.


Prove the corollary holds rather than trusting it: delete the new names from that arch's REGISTER_NAMES, rebuild the .so, and confirm the test fails on the guest-written assertion. A test that still passes with the export list reverted is asserting on a preset value. The x86 half (angr-2uw03: cs/ds/es/fs/gs/ss + ldt/gdt) was checked this way and failed at "ebx reads back 0x0" as required.

The sweep is now complete for ARM/AArch64 (angr-l8kfw), MIPS32/64 (angr-n2556) and x86 (angr-2uw03). x86 also settled where rule 4's line sits below the tail: guest_SC_CLASS records HOW a syscall was entered (int $0x80 / sysenter), not architectural state a guest instruction reads, so it stays alias-only alongside emnote/cmstart/cmlen/nraddr/ip_at_syscall.
invariant-arch-independent-reg-aliases: The architecture-independent register spellings in native/angr/src/arch/*.rs ALIASES tables are "sp", "bp" (angr-6qzik) and "pc" (angr-9ke6b.217) — all six arches now resolve all three. There is deliberately NO "ip" alias on ANY arch: on ARM the ABI calls r12 "ip", so exposing the ABI reading made a Python write through "ip" land in r12 instead of the PC (angr-itm3u). RustStateProxy._canonical_name rewrites "pc"/"ip" to the arch canonical name via archinfo before the name reaches Rust, so the Python path never depended on these; they exist for direct Rust-level / RustSimState.set_register callers. Gate: arch/registry_tests.rs::test_all_arches_report_expected_special_register_offsets asserts register_offset("pc") == ip_offset on every ALL_ARCHES row. NOTE tests/engines/rust/test_arch_offset_parity.py CANNOT catch a missing alias — its harness skips any archinfo name Rust does not know, so absent names are invisible there; only the Rust sweep sees them.
invariant-arch-register-tables: Per-arch register tables in native/angr/src/arch/{amd64,x86,arm,arm64,mips}.rs use CANONICAL: &[RegEntry] + ALIASES: &[RegEntry] const slices, where RegEntry = (name, offset, size_bytes). The lookup_register_{offset,size,name} helpers in arch/mod.rs and the impl_arch_registers!(canonical, aliases, names) macro drive the trait methods. CANONICAL drives register_name(offset) reverse lookups (one canonical name per offset); ALIASES holds sub-register names sharing an offset (e.g., 'eax' aliases 'rax' on amd64) and is consulted only by name->offset/size forward lookups. To add a new register: add ONE row in CANONICAL (if reverse-mappable) or ALIASES (if just a forward alias) -- but if the name is also in REGISTER_NAMES it MUST be CANONICAL, see invariant-register-names-subset-of-canonical (angr-9ke6b.9 moved X86's sseround/xmm0..7/fpreg/fptag/fpround/fc3210/ftop out of ALIASES for exactly this reason). The (name, offset, size) triplet is a single source of truth. ARM canonical uses sp/lr/pc (not r13/r14/r15t); ARM64 uses fp/lr/sp (not x29/x30/xsp); MIPS uses ABI mnemonics (zero/at/v0/...) not numeric rN. MIPS64 register_name is intentionally narrow (only zero/v0/a0/sp/fp/ra/pc reverse-mappable) -- preserved bug-for-bug. Arch trait methods (sp_offset, ip_offset, bp_offset, syscall_num_offset) live alongside the tables. NOTE (angr-9ke6b.216): Arch::argument_registers() and Arch::return_register() were DELETED -- they had zero callers and duplicated the CallingConvention tables. ABI arg/return registers now live only on CallingConvention impls, which reference the per-arch 'offsets' modules (now pub(crate)) by const name. NEVER hand-code 'match VexArch { ... => (offset, size) }' tables in callers -- they will silently drift. Always reach data through self.registers.arch() or arch_from_vex(arch).<method>(). If a needed lookup isn't on the trait, add a trait method, don't duplicate the match.
invariant-as-u128-some-for-constrained: RustBV::as_u128() returns Some for BOTH Concrete and Constrained (symbolic-with-known-value) leaves — see RustBV::as_u128 in symbolic/value.rs. Any op that folds via `match self.as_u128() { Some(v) => Self::concrete(v, ..) }` therefore DESTROYS RustBV::Constrained{id} and turns a still-symbolic value into a bare Concrete. Downstream that is a wrong answer, not an error: query_class, memory::ite_builder, memory::multi and interpreter::concretize_cache key off Constrained.id for symbol tracking / structural hashing / cache keys, and interpreter::exits + interpreter::statements special-case Constrained as 'concrete value but still symbolic'. RULE for any new conversion op: check the width/shape IDENTITY case and return self BEFORE calling as_u128(). zero_extend_into/sign_extend_into always did; truncate_into and drive_extract (value_ops.rs) did not until angr-9ke6b.128 (commit 2421919b7). Folding IS correct when the op actually changes the value (narrowing truncate, partial extract, real extension) — that is a new leaf, not the same symbol. Regression tests: identity_truncate_extract_preserve_constrained_id / narrowing_truncate_extract_fold_constrained_to_concrete in symbolic/value_serde_tests.rs; they build the Constrained via serde round-trip because snapshot deserialization (RustBVData::Constrained arm) is the ONLY live constructor.
invariant-assert-not-debug-assert-in-rel: Release-build invariant checks in native/angr/src/ must use assert!, not debug_assert!: the workspace [profile.release] does NOT set debug-assertions, so it defaults to false and every debug_assert! compiles out of the shipped .so. (angr-03vl4.84 armed debug-assertions in [profile.release-checked] — the CI rust_test / ralph-gate TEST profile — so a debug_assert! now at least gets *test* coverage; the shipped wheel still builds against plain release, so this rule is unchanged.) Found in angr-9ke6b.68 — scheduler.rs worker_thread's WorkerCtl::Run arm guarded the 'no !Send state parked across the coordinator boundary' invariant with debug_assert!, giving release builds zero protection (a violation would silently re-park stale states, no diagnostic trail). Rule of thumb: debug_assert! is fine only for hot-path checks whose violation is already caught elsewhere; any invariant whose violation causes silent corruption gets a real assert!. Cost is usually nil — this one is a VecDeque::is_empty per session-loop return and the fast-tier bench suite showed no delta. Pairs with panic-abort-no-poison-invariant: under panic='abort' an assert! is a loud SIGABRT at the violation site, which is the module's documented failure mode (scheduler.rs 'Panic policy' header). The follow-on sweep angr-9ke6b.220 applied this rule to the rest of the crate and recorded the per-site verdicts (which sites were promoted, and the five classes deliberately LEFT debug-only) in debug-assert-triage-policy — consult that before promoting anything new.

invariant-audit-gate-silence-is-not-abse: Regex audit gates (tools/audit_overflow_wraparound.py, audit_sp_default_zero.py, audit_rounding_mode_threading.py, audit_silent_fallback.py, audit_page_shift.py, check_line_citations.py) report 'OK, 0 new' whenever nothing matched their GRAMMAR — which is not the same as 'no such site exists'. RULE: when a bug is found by review inside a directory some gate already scans, treat the gate's silence as a second defect and widen the detector in the SAME commit — patching only the flagged site leaves the class open. Two confirmed instances, and note they are different KINDS of blind spot. (a) Incomplete grammar, angr-5mnx3.53: do_mmap's addr=0 align-up '(new_base & !PAGE_MASK) + PAGE_SIZE' was a real u64 overflow the gate never reported, because BINOP_RE's _OPERAND only matched identifier/dotted-field/numeric-literal and cannot begin an operand at ')'. (b) DELIBERATE exclusion, angr-fs8kb.52: BINOP_RE's '(?![=>])' lookahead was written to skip '+=' / '-=' / '->', so a stepped address 'page_addr += PAGE_SIZE' was invisible project-wide — which is how two page-walk wraparounds (angr-fs8kb.49, .51) landed in syscalls/ while it was fully scanned with an empty baseline. So also audit what a gate intentionally excludes, not only what its grammar happens to miss; a lookahead added for noise control is a silent scope cut. Four corollaries. (1) Every widening needs BOTH a must-fire and a must-NOT-fire control in the script's --self-test (the .52 widening added a stats-counter control and a '+=' whose address-shaped name is on the right). (2) A widening usually surfaces sites that were always there; expect to triage them in the same commit — .53's two hits already carried an 'overflow-ok:' rationale that fell just outside the three-line window, .52 surfaced 9 bounded loop counters needing fresh markers, and angr-fs8kb.91's new page-arithmetic gate surfaced 7 open-coded sites in state/export.rs + syscalls/cgc.rs + procedures/test_util.rs. (3) If naive widening is dominated by one benign shape, narrow by MEANING rather than abandoning it: the overflow gate's detector 2 keys on the compound assignment's DESTINATION name only (in 'a += b' the LHS is the accumulator) and on that name's LAST '_'-separated component, minus 'count' — 77 raw hits down to 9 real ones. audit_page_shift.py's detector 2 does the same for magic page literals: requiring the literal be ADJACENT TO AN OPERATOR whose other side is an address-shaped name drops every legitimate 'const MAX_...: usize = 4096;' buffer bound, because those sit to the right of an '='. (4) A prose sentence in a doc comment saying a class 'keeps coming back every audit round' (PageIndex's doc in memory/page.rs said exactly that across angr-c7xno.49 / angr-sqfj8.140 / angr-fs8kb.70) IS a gate that has not been written yet — treat that phrasing as the trigger to write one, not as documentation.
invariant-bare-push-pop-assumed-leak: Rust engine: bare SymContext::push()/pop() (transaction_ops.rs) restores the Z3 solver frame and scope_path but does NOT truncate local.assumed (the assumed export/re-assert log) — only transaction_rollback did. Any assume_true/assume_false made inside a bare push()/pop() scope leaks permanently into local.assumed. The deferred-fork block-feasibility loop in interpreter/statements.rs (prev-fork assert loop, popped at execution.rs block end) hit this: its feasibility-only assumes leaked and got re-asserted verbatim by restore_from_snapshot on wave migration (the spurious re-asserts angr-kenpr's constraint_count pin compensates for). FIX (commit 02ce2aae3, angr-ype54 iter34): SymContext::assumed_local_len + truncate_assumed_local bracket the loop. INVARIANT: if you add assume_* calls inside a bare push()/pop() (not a transaction), snapshot assumed_local_len first and truncate_assumed_local after, or they poison the export log. SIBLING FIX (angr-c7xno.75): the same loop also leaked into local.z3_assertions via fork()'s freeze — truncate_assumed_local only touches local.assumed. fork() now refuses to drain any local log while bare_local_savepoints is non-empty, so the z3_assertions half is closed at the fork gate rather than per-call-site. The assumed_local_len bracket is still required (it covers the export log independent of forking).
invariant-bare-z3-push-depth: Invariant for any future consumer of SymContext::bare_z3_push_depth (angr-3ms1 step 1a, revised angr-c7xno.75): the counter ONLY reflects pushes on THIS context's per-context Z3 solver (None lineage branch). It is always 0 along the Some (shared-lineage) branch, which records on scope_savepoints instead. Consequences: (1) the slice-1c fork-time materialization gate reads the *parent* counter at fork time — a non-zero value means parent has unbalanced bare pushes on its per-context solver, which would corrupt the shared lineage Z3 stack if a lineage were minted. (2) Children do NOT inherit the parent's value — fork() resets it to 0 (angr-c7xno.75, was inherited before). A child owns no open Z3 scopes: its bare_local_savepoints starts empty and SymContext::solver()'s cold-start replay emits flat assert()s, never push(). Inheriting a non-zero value made try_pop() (gated solely on this counter) forward a pop(1) to a never-pushed solver and permanently disqualified the child from lineage minting via gate (b). (3) When mixing Some and None paths (a context starts None, gets bare pushes, then has a lineage installed), the counter would still reflect the bare pushes — the gate should consider this case if it ever arises. Note this counter is NOT the 'is a scope open?' indicator: bare_local_savepoints is (it records on BOTH dispatch branches), and that is what fork()'s freeze gate and debug_assert_no_open_scope read.
invariant-bench-tier-vs-suite: run_regression.py's FAST_SUITE/MEDIUM_SUITE membership is a hand-maintained runtime-BUDGET split (fast <10s, medium 10-60s) and is deliberately NOT a mirror of the 'tier' field in run_single.EXAMPLE_CATALOG (fast <5s, medium 5-30s, gated by validate_tier.py + test_validate_tier.py). Six MEDIUM_SUITE members are catalog tier='fast' after the perf waves: sym-write, flareon2015_5, flareon2015_10, ekopartyctf2016_rev250, csaw_wyvern, codegate_2017-angrybird. Retiering a bench in the catalog must NOT move it between suites — 'syncing' the two would silently shrink what 'run_regression.py --full' gates. test_medium_suite_membership_is_independent_of_catalog_tier (tests/benchmarks/test_validate_tier.py) pins that set.
