invariant-bitcount-z3-operand-tied: The internal Z3 lowering (build_z3_ast_cached in native/angr/src/symbolic/value_z3.rs) and the claripy EXPORT path (build_sound_bitcount in native/angr/src/claripy_bridge/export/ast_helpers.rs, moved there by angr-5mnx3.11) are TWO separate lowerings of Clz/Ctz/Popcount that must stay in sync ON VALUE, not on structure. Both must build an operand-tied encoding: clz/ctz -> ITE ladder over per-bit tests, popcount -> sum of zero-extended bits. Never use z3 BV::new_const(name,width) for these: Z3 hash-conses named consts so every symbolic clz of a given width aliases to ONE shared unconstrained variable, making clz(x)==0 && clz(y)==5 UNSAT (prunes feasible branches) and letting eval(x) ignore the clz constraint. Fixed angr-ph300.29 (internal path); export path fixed earlier via test_lzcnt_symbolic_export_is_sound. Since angr-0jh0j.54 the two lowerings DIVERGE structurally: the Rust Z3 arm accumulates the ladder at bitcount_acc_width (ilog2(width)+1 bits) and zero_ext's once, because accumulating at the operand width is O(width^2) (width constants of width bits each, ~137 GiB at MAX_BV_WIDTH); build_sound_bitcount does not, and does not need to, because its caller already refuses width > 64. Keep the accumulator wide enough to hold the value 'width' itself -- clz/ctz of an all-zero operand IS width, and that is the only case a correctness test can distinguish, so any regression test for the sizing must pin an all-zero operand at a width above 64.
invariant-bounds-check-must-not-overflow: Overflow triage, bug shape the audit can't see: the BOUNDS CHECK itself is an overflow site when its index is wrapping-derived. SymbolicMemory::extract_byte_lane (memory/load.rs) guarded with '(byte_offset + 1) * 8 > total_bits'; both callers (assemble_load_with_multi, try_byte_merge_load) form byte_offset as '(byte_addr - base_addr) as u32', and Sub<Address> for Address is wrapping_sub — so a stale symbolic_spans entry whose base sits ABOVE the byte yields a near-u32::MAX offset, the product wraps to a small value with release overflow-checks off, the check PASSES, and the big-endian arm computes an underflowed 'total_bits - byte_offset*8 - 1'. Fixed by 'byte_offset.checked_add(1)?.checked_mul(8)?' — refuse, per invariant-overflow-fix-refuse-not-saturate-identities (an offset with no representable bit position IS out of range). Generalization: whenever an index crosses a wrapping boundary (Address diff, guest register, Python-supplied size), the guard that validates it must use checked_* even though the guarded expression looks safe once guarded. tools/audit_overflow_wraparound.py flags the guarded expression, never the guard, so an 'overflow-ok: guarded above' comment can silently bless a broken guard — read the guard before writing that comment. Regression: test_extract_byte_lane_refuses_wrapping_byte_offset (memory/tests/symbolic_wide.rs). Related: invariant-address-containment-wrapping-distance.
invariant-budget-cancel-vs-find-cancel: Wave-parallel cancel has TWO flavors and conflating them livelocks small run(n) calls (angr-9ke6b.52). CancelToken::cancel() = find/num_find/session-finalize: parallel_process_state's pre-step guard (run_loop.rs, the 'preempts_in_flight' branch) hands the state back UNSTEPPED so post-find speculation is not wasted. CancelToken::cancel_for_budget() = the wave dispatch budget (WorkTransport::max_dispatches, set by WaveJob::set_max_dispatches from run_loop_parallel_wave's remaining max_steps): the in-flight step MUST complete, because the dispatch was already charged to the budget. First attempt used plain cancel() for the budget and deadended_count went 14 -> 0 on tests/engines/rust/test_parallel_wave.py::test_deadended_count_survives_the_worker_boundary[4]: RustExplorationManager.run(n=N) maps to N native run(1) calls, so the wave budget is 1 -- a peer worker observed the budget spent and cancelled while the ONE worker that had dispatched was mid-step, which then bailed unstepped, so 4096 python-side steps advanced the manager by 4 steps total. Rule for any future 'stop the wave' signal: decide whether it should preempt already-dispatched work, and if not, route it through preempts_in_flight()==false.
invariant-budget-product-must-saturate: audit_overflow_wraparound.py scans bare +/- only, so a bare '*' on address/size operands is invisible to it. That blind spot matters because a wrapping *multiply* fails differently from a wrapping add: the add-side bug is a range check that wraps large, but a multiply can wrap to a value that is *small* (2^63 * 2 == 0), so a 'units * size > CAP' budget guard silently ACCEPTS an unbounded loop instead of refusing it. Rule: any product feeding a cap/budget comparison uses saturating_mul (saturating is correct here precisely because the saturated value is unambiguously over-cap and therefore refuses). Precedent: procedures/mem_common.rs::check_store_budget, shared by memset.rs::memset_symbolic_addr and memcpy.rs::copy_symbolic_addr. Companion to invariant-rust-concrete-arith-must-wrap (which covers +/- address arithmetic).
invariant-bv-cache-key-variant-tag: native/angr/src/interpreter/concretize_cache.rs::bv_cache_key routes EVERY RustBV variant through hash_bv (angr-9ke6b.89) — it does not shortcut Concrete to *value or Symbolic/Constrained to *id, and each arm hashes its FULL payload (angr-fs8kb.65). Rationale: untagged leaf shortcuts made Concrete{value:N} and Symbolic{id:N} share a u64 key. INVARIANT 1: keep the single hash_bv path — do not reintroduce a 'cheap' leaf shortcut for perf; the symbolic-leaf hash is a few ns against a Z3 concretize call and the bench gate showed no movement (22/22, 31.2s). INVARIANT 2 (the trap this function fell into twice): the 'all three call sites early-return on addr.as_u64(), so Concrete/Constrained can never reach here' argument scopes ONLY to the TOP-LEVEL value. hash_bv recurses into Expression operands, where those variants are routine — angr-owr37 dropped nested leaf identity by hashing 1 level, and angr-fs8kb.65 dropped Constrained's 'value' field under exactly that call-site justification, making Add(y,Constrained{id:5,value:10}) and Add(y,Constrained{id:5,value:20}) hash byte-identically (a guaranteed, not probabilistic, collision). Generalize: a call-site precondition NEVER justifies dropping a field from a RECURSIVE hash/key function. Regression tests: concretize_cache_tests.rs::bv_cache_key_distinguishes_leaf_variants_with_equal_scalars (top-level) and ::bv_cache_key_distinguishes_nested_constrained_values (nested).
invariant-byte-loop-writes-not-atomic: Rust native syscalls/procs that write a buffer with a byte-at-a-time `state.memory_store` loop (canonical: `syscalls/directory.rs::NativeGetcwdSyscall::call`) are intentionally NOT all-or-nothing: on a mid-buffer fault the bytes already stored stay committed and the handler returns -EFAULT. Do NOT 'fix' this into a rollback/staging buffer — it would diverge from both models we mirror. Real Linux `copy_to_user` keeps whatever it copied before the fault, and the Python SimProcedure's single `state.memory.store` (e.g. `procedures/linux_kernel/cwd.py::getcwd`) commits page by page before `SimSegfaultException` unwinds. A future audit round flagging one of these loops as a 'partial write bug' should document + pin it instead; `directory_tests.rs::getcwd_partial_write_is_not_rolled_back` is the pattern to copy. Corollary for callers: a -EFAULT return means the buffer is CLOBBERED, not preserved.
invariant-cache-key-covers-producer-conf: Rust-engine memoization caches must key on EVERYTHING the cached value depends on, not just the input expression. interpreter/concretize_cache.rs::bv_cache_key has now been the site of three separate wrong-answer bugs of exactly this shape: angr-owr37 (nested leaf identity dropped -> two distinct addresses collided), angr-9ke6b.89 (leaf variant untagged -> Concrete{value:N} vs Symbolic{id:N} collided), angr-360gt (producer CONFIG untagged -> a Multiple computed under read_range_limit=1024 was served to a store bound by write_range_limit=128, bypassing its Max fallback). The third is the subtle class: the key covered the input perfectly, but the cached value also depended on WHICH strategy chain produced it. Fix pattern: a namespace discriminant hashed into the key (see enum ConcretizeNs), not a post-hoc re-validation on hit — re-validation only works for shapes that carry their limit (TooLarge does; Multiple/Strided produced by the <=16 fast-enum path do not, since that path never consults the limit). When adding a new consumer to a shared cache, ask what config the entry was computed under; if it can differ, give it its own namespace.
invariant-calc-flags-sub-unmasked: All six x86/amd64 concrete ccall flag builders that take RAW operands — calc_flags_add, calc_flags_sub, calc_flags_adc, calc_flags_sbb, calc_flags_umul, calc_flags_smul (native/angr/src/vex/ccall/x86_concrete.rs) — now mask their operands to get_mask(nbits) BEFORE use, matching the symbolic siblings in x86_symbolic.rs which extract_to_nbits unconditionally. Add/sub got this under angr-36vvn.3; umul/smul under angr-0jh0j.69 (umul's hi = (prod >> nbits) & mask picked up cross-term corruption from garbage above the width, wrecking CF/OF; sign_extend_to_i64's non-negative branch returned val verbatim so nbits=8 val=0x100 multiplied as 256 instead of 0). SUPERSEDES the old claim that calc_flags_sub/add compare on raw u64 — they no longer do, and a diff-fuzz no longer needs to pre-mask to agree (the memory key still says 'unmasked' only so existing citations keep resolving). ccall_tests.rs::diff_fuzz_sym_flags_unmasked_inputs is the gate: it diffs concrete vs symbolic over Add/Sub/Adc/Sbb/Logic/Umul/Smul with UNMASKED random operands and also pins that masking the inputs changes nothing. When adding a new concrete flag builder that takes raw operands, mask first and extend that test's category list — every other diff_fuzz_sym_flags_* pre-masks and cannot see this bug class.
invariant-callback-fields-single-source: PythonCallbacks (native/angr/src/callbacks/mod.rs) has ONE source of truth for its Option<Py<PyAny>> callback slots: the with_callback_fields! macro, which expands to $m!{field, field, ...}. new(), traverse_fields and clear_fields are all generated from it via local macro_rules! consumers (empty_holder / visit_fields / clear_all), and since angr-0jh0j.6 so is every set_<slot> PyO3 setter, via the angr_macros::callback_setters! proc macro (driven as `with_callback_fields!(callback_setters PythonCallbacks =>)`; it emits its OWN #[pymethods] impl block because an attribute proc macro cannot see through an unexpanded macro_rules! invocation inside one). So adding a callback is exactly TWO places: the struct definition (doc comment + type) and that list -- the Python-visible setter follows for free. Per-slot prose (expected Python signature, degraded paths, confusable siblings) belongs on the struct FIELD's doc comment, which the generated setter doc links to. WHY it matters: traverse_fields and clear_fields back __traverse__/__clear__ on BOTH PythonCallbacks and RustExplorationManager (which holds a clone). A slot present in one list but not the other, or missing from both, silently keeps the mgr -> _callbacks -> bound method -> mgr reference cycle alive and leaks the manager plus its _state_cache (~4030 angr pages/call on mma_howtouse -- the 9maq leak). ENFORCEMENT is compile-time, not a test: clear_fields destructures 'let Self { ... } = self' EXHAUSTIVELY, deliberately without a '..' rest pattern, so a field added to the struct but not the list has no binding and fails to build. Do NOT 'fix' that by adding '..' -- that silently disarms the guard. Self-tested (angr-9ke6b.27) by adding a probe field to the struct alone: E0063 from the new() expansion + 'pattern requires .. due to inaccessible fields' from the clear destructure. The non-Py Arc fields (inspect_enabled, memory_is_rust_proxy, python_servable_pages, python_page_universe) are named explicitly in the destructure (three as ': _') for the same reason. Runtime half pinned by callbacks_tests.rs::clear_fields_drops_every_callback_slot. [Deliberately states NO slot count: an earlier revision of this memory cited '34' against an actual 30 -- a live instance of the cardinality-drift anti-pattern this convention warns about elsewhere (lane_traits.rs / CLAUDE.md). Cite the with_callback_fields! list by name, never by count.]
invariant-callback-slot-names-are-not-re: PythonCallbacks naming beads (e.g. angr-9ke6b.29) should be closed with DOCS, not renames: each `call_<x>` / `has_<x>` / `set_<x>` in native/angr/src/callbacks/{dispatch,mod}.rs is keyed to a Python callback SLOT of the same name, wired by rust_manager.py::_setup_callbacks and asserted by name in error strings ('<x> callback not set') that tests match on. Renaming the Rust side alone desyncs the trio from the slot and breaks grep-by-slot-name; renaming both ends is a Python-surface change for a readability win. The canonical example: the three symbolic-store variants now carry a selector list in the dispatch.rs module doc — `call_memory_store_symbolic_value` = concrete address + AST data, `call_memory_store_symbolic_full` = symbolic address (data either), and bare `call_memory_store_symbolic` is NOT a third mode, it forwards to _full and hard-errors when _full is unwired (angr-ph300.64).
invariant-cargo-test-cannot-lift-blocks: Rust unit tests (cargo test, default features) CANNOT lift a VEX block. The native lifter is behind the libvex-ffi feature, which is deliberately NOT in Cargo.toml's `default` set (setup.py appends it, so pip/CI builds have it but `cargo test` does not). Without it, VEXInterpreter block lifting routes through the unregistered Python `lift_block` callback and fails. CONSEQUENCE for test design: a #[cfg(test)] test that wants to drive run_interpreter_step_core / parallel_process_state to a post-step outcome (CoreReturn::Continue/Deadended/Errored/Unconstrained) would assert a DIFFERENT thing depending on the feature set — do not write one. What IS reachable without a lifter: a hooked/simproc'd initial pc, which short-circuits before any lift and yields CoreReturn::NeedsPython (BounceKind::Hook / SimProcedurePython). Post-step arm classification is instead unit-tested directly on run_post_step_core (core_outcome_tests/, split per RunResult arm); the worker's routing of them is covered by the Python tests/engines/rust/ parallel suite. Precedent + rationale live in the module headers of step_core_tests.rs and run_loop_worker_tests.rs.
invariant-ccall-arch-sibling-symbolic-pa: CCall symbolic dispatch drifts BETWEEN ARCH SIBLINGS, not just between builder and consumer. Since the angr-5mnx3.60 helper split, native/angr/src/vex/ccall/mod.rs::handle_ccall_with_ctx is pure name dispatch and the near-identical arm pairs are sibling helper FUNCTIONS — handle_arm32_condition/flags_nzcv/flag_single vs handle_arm64_*, handle_x86_calculate_condition/eflags_c/eflags_all covering both x86g_* and amd64g_*. A symbolic branch added to one sibling is repeatedly never mirrored onto the other: angr-0jh0j.70 found armg_calculate_flag_n/z/c/v concrete-only while arm64g_calculate_flag_* had had its symbolic branch all along, even though arm_sym_flag_n/z/c/v already existed in ccall/arm32.rs and were already used by arm_sym_calculate_condition in the same file. INVARIANT: when touching any handle_* helper, grep the sibling-arch CCall name and confirm both have the same concrete+symbolic structure; a missing symbolic branch is a silent ~30x wall-clock Python fallback (angr-9ke6b.88), not a visible error. angr-zgd3r closed the last known ARM gap by adding arm_sym_flags_nzcv / arm64_sym_flags_nzcv — note it fixed BOTH siblings in one commit, which is the shape to aim for. Corollary from that fix: a packed-flags symbolic path must refuse a ret_bits too narrow to hold its top shift (sym_pack_nzcv returns None for ret_bits <= SHIFT_N) — RustBV shift amounts are built at the result width and would wrap silently. Anchor tests on the coverage pattern (iterate the whole cc_op range, assert nothing returns None) plus a z3-gated diff-fuzz that pins a symbolic dep with add_bv_constraint and compares ctx.eval against the concrete calculator — see arm32_flag_ccalls_symbolic_cover_every_cc_op / diff_fuzz_arm_flags_nzcv_symbolic_matches_concrete in vex/ccall_tests.rs. Related: invariant-symflags-category-coverage (the builder-vs-consumer half of the same family).
invariant-ccall-flag-mask-named-constant: Symbolic ccall flag masks must reuse the same named G_CC_MASK_* constants as the concrete calculate_eflags_all path, never a hand-derived hex literal. In vex/ccall/mod.rs the symbolic CC_OP_COPY branch (handle_x86_eflags_all since the angr-5mnx3.60 helper split; inline in handle_ccall_with_ctx before it) had drifted to 0xD5 (C,P,A,Z,S) while the concrete Copy path used O|S|Z|P|C|A = 0x8D5, silently zeroing the Overflow bit (0x800) for symbolic-operand COPY cc_ops — a silent wrong-answer on OF branches. Fixed angr-36vvn.1 by masking with the constants. Rule: any flag-mask literal duplicated across the concrete+symbolic ccall paths is a drift hazard.
invariant-ccall-guest-width-truncation: INVARIANT (ccall guest-width truncation): a sub-64-bit guest's ccall flag helper computes in u64, so it MUST mask both its dep inputs and the arithmetic result to the guest width before extracting a flag bit. The dispatch site's RustBV::concrete(result, ret_bits) does NOT rescue an unmasked helper — it truncates 0x1FFFFFFFF to 0xFFFFFFFF, i.e. turns garbage into different garbage instead of erroring. angr-03vl4.72: vex/ccall/arm32.rs::armg_calc_flag_n was the lone ARM32 per-flag helper without it, so ARMG_CC_OP_SUB with dep1=0,dep2=1 returned 0xFFFFFFFF for the N flag instead of 1, live on the standalone armg_calculate_flag_n CCall arm (taken whenever all four args are concrete). Its siblings armg_calc_flag_z/_c/_v mask on entry and mask each wrapping_* result; arm64 gets it for free via the shared arm64_res helper. When adding or reviewing a per-flag helper for a 32-bit guest, check BOTH masks — entry-only masking still lets a borrowing subtract sign-extend into the high half. Sibling rule: [invariant-ccall-flag-mask-named-constants].
invariant-ccall-unsupported-fallback: expressions_arith.rs eval_ccall fallback contract (UPDATED angr-9ke6b.88, commit 68d7ad34a — supersedes the pre-2026-08-01 'fabricate is sound' rule). handle_ccall_with_ctx==None now has TWO outcomes, not three: (1) calculate_condition/eflags/rflags → Err(NeedPythonFallback) BY DEFAULT; a fresh unconstrained symbolic is fabricated ONLY when ANGR_RUST_FABRICATE_UNSUPPORTED_IROP is set (same OnceLock gate as vex_op_fallback; bumps vex_bypass_fabricate_count). Rationale: the result of *_calculate_condition IS a branch guard, so an unconstrained stand-in explores both directions regardless of real flag semantics — strictly worse than the ordinary-IROp case angr-oyzvj already made opt-in. (2) any other CCall → Err(NeedPythonFallback), mapped by execution.rs to RunResult::NeedPythonVEX → _handle_python_vex_fallback. NEVER return concrete(0) on the fallthrough. Regression test: eval_ccall_unsupported_cond_routes_to_python_not_fabricate in interpreter/expressions_tests.rs (negation-verify by running it with ANGR_RUST_FABRICATE_UNSUPPORTED_IROP=1). GENERALIZED (angr-c7xno.44, 2026-08-09): this is now the crate-wide policy for EVERY site that would stand in an unconstrained symbolic for a value it cannot compute — there are three, all sharing the one OnceLock gate expressions_arith.rs::fabricate_unsupported_irop (pub(super) since c7xno.44) and the vex_bypass_fabricate_count counter: vex_op_fallback's any_sym arm, eval_ccall's condition-flag arm, and statements_dirty.rs::handle_dirty_call's !callbacks.has_dirty_call() arm. A NEW fabrication site must join them (gate + counter + a routes-to-python-not-fabricate test) rather than fabricating ungated. handle_dirty_call's test is statements_dirty_tests.rs::unmodelled_dirty_call_routes_to_python_not_fabricate.
invariant-check-branch-feasibility-not-c: SymContext::can_be_true(c) and can_be_false(c) are each literally check_branch_feasibility(c).0/.1 (native/angr/src/symbolic/solving_ops.rs, vex-engine-z3 arm), so calling BOTH on the same condition pays two full feasibility queries — two solver acquisitions, two Z3_BRANCH_* counter ticks, and the model-cache shortcut applied twice — where one call answers both directions under a single lock. Any site that needs the (can_be_true, can_be_false) pair must call check_branch_feasibility once, never the can_be_* pair. Fixed at the guarded-load/store handlers in angr-12jjk.22 (VEXInterpreter::classify_guard in interpreter/statements.rs is now the shared entry point for every guarded statement's tristate; GuardClass::from_feasibility folds the pair).
invariant-chunked-concrete-memory-read: angr-9ke6b.230 (commit a0846d97f): the u128 chunk helpers now live in native/angr/src/symbolic/bv_chunk.rs (re-exported from symbolic::), NOT exploration/helpers.rs — they were sunk one layer so state/pymethods.rs (which must not import exploration/) can use them too. Four fns + MAX_CONCRETE_CHUNK=16: store_concrete_bytes_chunked, load_concrete_bytes_chunked, u128_to_le_bytes, u128_le_byte; all generic over the error type E so symbolic/ takes no pyo3 dep (pymethods sites use E=PyErr). INVARIANT: any concrete bulk memory read/write wider than 16 bytes MUST go through them — RustBV::Concrete is u128-backed, so as_u128()/u128_to_le_bytes only round-trip 16 bytes and a wider single op truncates, wraps mod 128 into a repeating pattern, or (read side) fails as 'symbolic' on a fully-concrete region. The five call sites: state_api::_get_state_memory + _set_state_memory_concrete, pending_api::_get_pending_memory + _pending_memory_load + _pending_memory_store/_set_pending_memory, state/pymethods.rs::{memory_load,memory_store}. Callers do their with_state/with_pending lookup ONCE outside the helper and read inside that single borrow; do not resurrect the old per-chunk recursive self-call. Behavioral split to preserve: _get_pending_memory is deliberately eval-free (angr-04tw3.2), while _get_state_memory and _pending_memory_load concretize a symbolic load to a SAT witness. _get_state_memory keeps its Option contract with a closure-local sentinel PyErr so a missing state_id is still Err, not Ok(None). Tests live in symbolic/bv_chunk_tests.rs. GOTCHA (angr-0jh0j.1/.2, commit 11817904e): the ceiling is NOT memory-specific — it bit the REGISTER file too. arch/register_file.rs's RegisterFile::get/put composed a whole register into one u128, and x86/amd64 'fpreg' is 64 bytes; the name-keyed get_reg/put_reg reach it even though register_names() excludes it for exactly this width. When scanning for this bug class, the question is 'does any u128 shift index come from a caller-supplied byte count?', not 'is this the memory subsystem?'. The two fix shapes, both now canonical: a >16-byte READ has no Concrete representation at all — build it with concat (RegisterFile::compose_range), which declines to fold past 128 bits and stays exact as a Concat tree, and let as_u128()==None give the Python caller a clean error; a >16-byte WRITE of a wide Concrete extracts bytes via u128_le_byte, whose zeros above the payload ARE the value (a >128-bit Concrete is its low bits zero-extended), never a wrapped repeat. Second-order gotcha: tests that infer a register's size behaviorally by diffing get_registers_raw() after a set_register write (tests/engines/rust/test_arch_offset_parity.py::_rust_offset_size) can only observe 16 bytes once the wrap is fixed — cap the expectation at the probe's reach (_PROBE_MAX_BYTES), do not read the shrinking span as offset-table drift.
invariant-clone-provenance-not-name-stri: Provenance of a cloned struct must be a flag stamped at its mint site, never inferred from a name/path string field. Closed angr-tqw60 (2026-09-08): FileSystem::fd0_is_dup2d asked 'is fd 0 still the pristine stdin placeholder?' by comparing FileDescriptor::name against "/dev/stdin", but FileSystem::open stores the caller's path verbatim and dup2 clones the whole descriptor, so a guest open("/dev/stdin")+dup2(fd,0) produced a clone the check read as pristine -- native stdin readers kept minting fresh unconstrained bytes over the guest's real content (silently wrong). Fix: FileDescriptor::is_std_placeholder, set ONLY by FileDescriptor::new_std_placeholder which only FileSystem::default's three std fds use; never by open/open_with_content/open_symbolic/register_fd_at/pipe. The same heuristic had been copy-pasted into Python (_inject_rust_fds in angr/exploration/rust_callback_dispatch.py); it now asks Rust via RustExplorationManager::state_fd0_is_dup2d, because the get_state_open_fds tuple carries no provenance signal and widening it would break every unpack site. Two lessons: (1) when a native check has a Python mirror, fix both in the same change or the bounce path re-introduces the bug; (2) for a new #[serde(default)] provenance field, pick the polarity whose legacy-snapshot default lands on the conservative side (here false => 'treat as dup2'd' => bounce to the reference Python impl, never a wrong answer).
invariant-coalesce-fingerprint: Phase 4.2 flush_multi_cells (multi.rs::flush_multi_cells) coalesces runs of adjacent Multi bytes ONLY when payload_cond_fingerprint() matches across consecutive addresses. For RustBV::Expression the fingerprint mixes Arc::as_ptr identity of the operands with a hash of the BVOp (angr-03vl4.38); the pointer half relies on install_multi_for_candidates building one cond RustBV per candidate then cloning into each byte (so neighbours from the same store-call share the same Arc), and on value_ops::expr_node allocating a fresh operands Arc per node. Any new store path that emits Multi bytes MUST follow this 'build cond once, clone into each byte' pattern, or it will silently fall back to the per-byte flush path (correctness preserved, perf loss). Run length is capped at COALESCE_MAX_RUN=16 because RustBV::concat_into's u128 concrete fast-path silently truncates widths >120+8. Lift the cap only after auditing concat_into for wider-than-128 safety.
invariant-concrete-bv-u128-16-byte-limit: RustBV::Concrete stores its value in a u128 (16 bytes / 128 bits max) regardless of declared width. Four hazard families follow. (1) ASSEMBLY: any code that ASSEMBLES a concrete value wider than 16 bytes by funneling bytes through a u128 is BUGGY: the shift wraps mod 128 in release (panics in debug), OR-ing high bytes back over low bytes. Fixed sites (commit df4bb4cd3, bd angr-tk7yv): memory/load.rs::load_concrete (two copies -- eager + lazy paths) now assemble size>16 loads as a Concat of per-byte concretes; symbolic/value_ops.rs::concat_into AND concat_no_ctx now guard the concrete-fold with 'if result_width <= 128' (else keep a Concat expression); exploration/state_api.rs::_get_state_memory reads in <=16-byte chunks. Also interpreter/bv_utils.rs::bytes_to_bv (angr-03vl4.31, commits 7608c8814 + 00b619214) -- the VEX-side twin of memory/load.rs::bytes_to_bv, reached from expressions.rs load fast paths, mod.rs read_memory and statements_dirty.rs::handle_dirty_call; it folds >16-byte inputs into a Concat via concat_no_ctx (high byte first: a.concat(b) puts a above b). Also interpreter/expressions.rs::eval_const's IRConst::V256 arm (angr-03vl4.29, commit 6ac725232) -- it packed v[0]|v[1]<<64 into ONE concrete tagged width 128, dropping v[2]/v[3]; now high.concat_no_ctx(&low) of the two 128-bit halves. Note the acceptance criteria said 'just retag the width as 256', which alone would have kept the truncation -- a wide width tag on a Concrete is a LIE, not a fix. Symptom seen: get_state_memory(24) on xmllint rodata returned chunk0|chunk2. Affects 32-byte AVX (ymm) concrete loads too. INVARIANT for future code: never pack >16 concrete bytes into a u128; build wide concretes via per-byte/per-chunk Concat, and do NOT 'fix' the overflow by clamping at 16 bytes -- that trades an abort for a silently truncated value. (2) BIT-SLICING (was invariant-concrete-extract-width128): bits at position >= 128 of a wider-than-128 Concrete (e.g. a 192-bit Multi-cell value) are logically zero, and RustBV::as_u128() returns Some for ANY Concrete width. Any bit-slicing on a concrete fast path (e.g. extract_into in symbolic/value_ops.rs) MUST guard BOTH: shift-by-low (v >> low overflows when low >= 128 -> result is 0) AND mask (1u128 << result_width overflows at result_width >= 128 -> use u128::MAX). Fixed in angr-dondi; mirrors the same width>=128 mask guard already in RustBV::concrete() (value.rs). (3) VEC-OP WIDENING (angr-sqfj8.118): adding 256-bit lane shapes to a vex/opcode_map*.rs parse arm (vector shapes live in opcode_map_vector.rs) silently makes that op's evaluator concrete fast path reachable at total_width=256, where 'result |= lane << lo' shifts a u128 by up to 192. Before widening ANY vector op family to V256, check its evaluator carries the 'if total_width <= 128' guard that vec_int_lane_op (ops/vec_int_lane.rs) has -- vec_shift_n (ops/vec_shift.rs; the merged shift-by-immediate helper that replaced vec_shl_n/vec_shr_n/vec_sar_n in angr-5mnx3.68) did not until .118. Applied again in angr-sqfj8.112 (V256 CmpEQ/CmpGT): vec_int_lane_op's existing guard is why that widening needed no evaluator change. The float lane ops were the last V256 op-coverage gap and are now covered too (angr-fs8kb.15, ops/tests_vec_float_lane.rs::test_vec_float_binops_avx2_256_bit_f32x8 and ::test_vec_float_min_max_sqrt_avx2_256_bit_f64x4); vec_float_lane_op's 'if total_width <= 128' guard was already present and correct. (4) SERIALIZATION (angr-03vl4.4): the reverse direction, RustBV -> bytes, has the mirror overflow ('value >> (i*8)' for i up to 31). interpreter/bv_utils.rs::bv_to_bytes stops at 16 bytes and zero-fills above, which IS correct there because as_u128() only ever exposes the low 128 bits -- but it means bv_to_bytes CANNOT serialize a wide Concat (as_u128() is None -> it returns all zeros); the reject_symbolic_byte_store guard is what keeps that from silently zeroing memory. callbacks/dispatch.rs used to carry a byte-identical private copy of bv_to_bytes that inherited every bug; it now imports interpreter::bv_utils::bv_to_bytes (which is pub(crate) for exactly that reason). Test pattern for a >128-bit op: build operands with concat_into of two 128-bit concretes and assert one extracted lane at a time (ops/tests_vec_int_lane.rs::test_vec_cmp_avx2_256_bit_i32x8); for the byte conversions see interpreter/bv_utils_tests.rs::bytes_to_bv_of_256_bit_buffer_keeps_every_byte_via_concat.
invariant-concrete-bv-width128-shift-gua: RustBV concrete fast-paths that shift/mask a u128 by a bit position (not an operand-supplied amount) must guard for width>128: a Concrete stores its value in a u128, so any bit >=128 is logically zero, and shifting a u128 by >=128 is a debug abort / release mod-128 wrap. Canonical guards live in extract_into (value_ops.rs): shift=0 when low>=128, mask=u128::MAX when result_width>=128; concat_into keeps result_width>128 as a Concat expr instead of folding. extract_no_ctx had the same window logic but WITHOUT the guards until angr-ph300.31 -> aborted/mis-extracted on 256-bit ymm sub-register overlays (arch/register_file.rs extract_no_ctx callers). Any new concrete BV op that shifts by a bit position must copy extract_into's guards. Complements [[invariant-concrete-shift-clamp-before-narrow]] which covers operand-amount narrowing.
invariant-concrete-shift-clamp-before-na: Concrete shift/rotate arms in RustBV (value_ops.rs shl_into/lshr_into/ashr_into and define_rotate_pair! -> rotl_into/rotr_into) must reduce/clamp the shift amount BEFORE narrowing u128->u32. A pre-narrow "a as u32" truncates amounts>=2^32 to their low 32 bits (2^32 reads as 0), diverging from the Z3/symbolic arms which compare the full-width amount. Also: shl/lshr by width==128 wraps wrapping_shl(128) to a no-op (guard amt>=w -> 0); rotl/rotr with amt%w==0 must special-case (else v>>(w-amt) shifts a u128 by 128 = debug abort under panic=abort). ashr saturates to sign for amt>=w (clamp to w-1). Any new binop that narrows an amount to u32 must match its symbolic arm semantics for out-of-range amounts. WIDTH>128 RULE (angr-03vl4.59, commit 31df03cb7): a Concrete may declare width up to 256 while storing only the low 128 bits (see invariant-concrete-bv-u128-16-byte-limit), so every concrete fast path needs a width>128 story -- but "add the width.min(128) clamp the siblings have" is NOT always that story. Split by whether the true wide result is representable in the low 128 bits: lshr/ashr out-of-range results are all-zero, so they ARE representable and the clamp is right (a right shift can only shrink the represented magnitude); shl is the exception (angr-fs8kb.25) -- it GROWS the magnitude, so both halves of the old width.min(128) clamp were wrong at width>128: an amount in [128,width) is an in-range shift with a nonzero result, not a full shift-out, and even an in-range amount can push v's own high bits past bit 127. shl_into now cuts off at the true a>=width and otherwise folds only when the free fn exact_shl says the result fits the payload, declining to an Expression like rotate/reverse do; a non-trivial rotate moves set bits to positions >=128 that the u128 payload cannot hold, so there is NO correct concrete answer and the fold must be DECLINED (fall through to expr_node, keeping the op symbolic -- same choice concat_into/concat_no_ctx make for a wide concat). reverse_owned joined the declined-fold group in angr-03vl4.60 (commit ec6b2d264): a byte reverse moves byte 0 to bit position w-8 >= 128, likewise unstorable. Ask "is the wide answer storable?" before reaching for a clamp; clamping an unstorable result silently truncates (the same mistake the first angr-03vl4.31 commit made in bytes_to_bv). Wide coverage lives in value_ops_property_tests.rs WIDE_WIDTHS tests (wide_rotate_declines_the_concrete_fold, wide_reverse_declines_the_concrete_fold, wide_shl_declines_the_fold_when_bits_escape_the_payload).
invariant-concrete-width-gt-128-fast-pat: A RustBV::Concrete stores its value in a u128 but may legitimately carry width>128 (bits>=128 are logically zero; zero_extend_into/truncate_into fast paths return concrete(v, to_width) for ANY to_width). So the concrete fast-path ops in value_ops.rs must stay correct for width>128, NOT just <=128. FOUR distinct hazards. (1) OVERFLOW/WRAP when shifting or masking a u128 by a width or bit-position (angr-qwyti.12): lshr_into cuts off at a>=width.min(128) (a right shift only SHRINKS the magnitude, so an out-of-range amount really does clear every readable bit); shl_into does NOT -- see hazard (3), it cuts off at the true a>=width and declines the fold whenever the shift would push a set bit to position >=128; ashr_into at width>128 collapses to lshr and guards amt>=128; sign_extend_to returns value early when from_width>=128 (avoids 1u128<<(from_width-1)). Same class as invariant-concrete-bv-u128-16-byte-limit / invariant-concrete-shift-clamp-before-narrow / sar_fill_mask (qwyti.17). (2) SIGN SEMANTICS (angr-03vl4.58): at width>128 the true sign bit (pos width-1>=128) is beyond the storage, so the value is logically NON-NEGATIVE and every SIGNED fast path must degenerate to its unsigned sibling -- signed compare to unsigned compare, bvsdiv/bvsrem to bvudiv/bvurem. Predicate sign_bit_beyond_storage(width) in value_ops.rs single-sources this; the fn sign_extend (u128->i128 helper feeding define_signed_cmp_pair!/sdiv/srem) must NOT be reached there and debug_asserts it, because past 128 bits the logical value can exceed i128::MAX and is not representable in i128 at all -- 'treat it as non-negative' is not expressible in the return type, the CALLER owes the unsigned branch. (3) UNREPRESENTABLE RESULT (angr-0jh0j.51/.52/.53, round 5; earlier angr-03vl4.59/.60 for rotate/reverse): the fold's true answer needs a bit in [128..width) that the payload cannot store, so folding emits a DIFFERENT number, not a truncated one -- e.g. (2^128-1)+1 at width 200 folded to 0, NOT of a wide zero folded to 2^128-1, sign-extending a 32-bit -1 to 200 bits folded to a NON-NEGATIVE 2^128-1. The only correct move is to DECLINE the fold and return an Expression node (Z3 then computes it exactly at the declared width). Predicate bits_beyond_storage(width) single-sources the ceiling test (sign_bit_beyond_storage delegates to it); concrete_arith_fits(width, checked_result) is the add/sub/mul form (and, via the free fn exact_shl, the shl form -- u128::checked_shl reports only an out-of-range AMOUNT, never a bit shifted off the top, so shl needs its own exact-result helper) -- below the ceiling a carry across bit 127 IS the mandated mod-2^width wrap, above it the carry is a real result bit. sign_extend_to returns Option<u128> so it can decline. (4) SATURATED CONSTANT (angr-nknv1): RustBV::all_ones_mask(width) and RustBV::ones(width) both SATURATE at width>=128 -- they yield 2^128-1, which above 128 bits is an ordinary number, not the width's all-ones value (unrepresentable in the payload). So (a) never test 'is this operand all-ones' with a bare `v == Self::all_ones_mask(w)` -- use the free fn is_all_ones(v, width), which ANDs in !bits_beyond_storage; the and_into `x & all_ones -> x` and or_into `x | all_ones -> all_ones` arms fired on 2^128-1 and, with a SYMBOLIC operand, respectively kept bits [128..w) the AND must clear and dropped bits the OR must keep. (b) never MATERIALISE Self::ones(w) on a path a wide width reaches -- udiv/sdiv's total `x / 0 -> all-ones` fold now declines via a `b != 0 || !bits_beyond_storage(w)` arm guard (Z3 bvudiv/bvsdiv are total the same way). Audit any new Self::ones caller (exploration/core_outcome_cc.rs::write_syscall_return is fine: register width <=64). Declining is ALWAYS safe (correctness over folding); the ops that legitimately still fold wide are and/or/xor of two CONCRETES (bitwise ops on two logically-high-zero payloads are exact), -0, mul-by-0, x%0, rotate-by-multiple-of-width, and any add/sub/mul whose checked_* is Some. Deterministic tests: WIDE_WIDTHS block in value_ops_property_tests.rs (wide_shl_*/wide_lshr_*/wide_ashr_*/wide_sign_extend_*/wide_signed_compare_degenerates_to_unsigned/wide_sdiv_srem_degenerate_to_unsigned/wide_rotate_declines_the_concrete_fold/wide_reverse_declines_the_concrete_fold/wide_arith_declines_the_fold_when_the_result_leaves_the_payload/wide_not_and_neg_decline_the_concrete_fold/wide_sign_extend_of_negative_source_declines_the_concrete_fold/wide_and_or_against_saturated_all_ones_decline_the_simplification/wide_div_by_zero_declines_the_concrete_fold).
invariant-concretize-cache-shared-across: The interpreter's per-block `concretize_cache` (interpreter/concretize_cache.rs, cleared at the top of execution.rs::execute_block_with_callbacks) is SHARED by three entry points with three different strategy chains — concretize_cached_read (Range(read_range_limit) -> Any), concretize_cached_write (Range(write_range_limit) -> Max, or Max-only when SYMBOLIC_WRITE_ADDRESSES is off), and concretize_cached_jump (plain AddressConcretizer::concretize = read-limit chain, NO fallback; added angr-9ke6b.92 for exits.rs::eval_next_addr). Sharing one map across mismatched chains is sound for the Single case for a non-obvious reason: every fallback Single is produced via concretize::pin_fallback_addr, which does ctx.assume_true(addr == chosen) — a REAL solver constraint, not a local pick. So once any variant has cached a fallback Single, a fresh concretize on the same expression is forced to return that same Single anyway. Non-Single shapes (Multiple/Strided/TooLarge) differ only in which range limit produced them, and each caller re-applies its own fallback on cache HIT (jump has none by design: eval_next_addr turns any non-Single into CbExecutionError::Unsupported and defers to Python rather than pinning an arbitrary jump target). INVARIANT for a fourth entry point: it may share the cache only if (a) its Single results are pin-backed and (b) it re-applies its own fallback on HIT rather than trusting the stored shape. Keying is bv_cache_key, which must stay a FULL recursive op-tree hash (angr-owr37) — a shallow key silently cross-wires addresses.
invariant-concurrency-test-needs-barrier: Concurrency regression tests over scheduler helpers need an explicit std::sync::Barrier to have any signal. test_absorb_continues_cap_holds_under_concurrent_workers (exploration/scheduler_worker_tests.rs) first spawned W threads under std::thread::scope with no gate and PASSED against the known-buggy check-then-act absorb_continues -- thread spawn is slow enough that each worker finished its whole load-decide-add before the next started, so the race never occurred. Building the states BEFORE the barrier and releasing all workers together makes the pre-fix shape fail within the first couple of rounds (32 rounds x 4 workers x 8 forks, ~0.4s). Rule: a concurrency test must be shown to FAIL with the fix reverted (git checkout the production file, run, restore) -- otherwise it is a coin flip that only ever documents the fixed behavior.
invariant-config-broadcast-covers-pendin:
A manager-level BROADCAST mutator (one that loops self.sm.stashes_mut(), or just STASH_ACTIVE, to push something onto every live state) must ALSO reach the TWO buckets of live RustSimStates that live in NO stash: (1) self.pending_callbacks — pending.state plus pending.pre_callback_snapshot (the fork_base deferred forks are materialized from), and (2) self.pending_parallel_bounces — the bounce queue a wave/session pass left undispatched. Since angr-0jh0j.82 there IS one helper that spans all three buckets: RustExplorationManager::all_live_states / all_live_states_mut (exploration/run_loop.rs), plus non_stash_live_states_mut for a broadcast that deliberately covers only some stashes (_active_states_map_memory maps into STASH_ACTIVE only). Reach for those, not a hand-rolled .chain().chain() — the three bucket lines differ only by method name, so a copy that drops one still compiles. A parked state is in no stash and nothing re-applies the change on resume, so it keeps the old value forever, as do its deferred forks. Bitten four times: set_deterministic (angr-sqfj8.32) and set_max_history (angr-c7xno.21) vs pending_callbacks, _active_states_map_memory (angr-03vl4.23) vs pending_callbacks, then all THREE of those vs pending_parallel_bounces (angr-03vl4.10) — so it is NOT only a config-knob rule: any broadcast over live states qualifies, including a memory mapping. Neither #[angr_macros::steady_guarded] nor its compile-time impl-block coverage check (#[angr_macros::steady_guard_checked], which replaced the retired tools/audit_steady_guard_coverage.py script) covers this: both only prove SOME call to steady_config_guard() happened, which drains the parallel session's resident frontier — they say nothing about the parked-state buckets, which remain a SEPARATE, unautomated obligation. The one carrier all_live_states does NOT reach is fork_snapshots (BranchSnapshot carries solver + registers + memory, nothing else), because it is not a RustSimState; a caller chains its own pending_callbacks loop for it. Which flavor needs it: a solver-flavored broadcast does (constraints::apply_fork_snapshots_deterministic — narrowed in angr-0jh0j.82 to exactly that carrier, since all_live_states now covers the two RustSimState halves it used to also touch), a memory-flavored one does (_active_states_map_memory maps into snapshot.memory), a plain state-struct-field knob like max_history does not; pending_parallel_bounces entries are bare (RustSimState, BounceKind, u64) tuples, so they need no carrier walk at all. NOTE the broadcast/census asymmetry: all_live_states/parked_bounce_states yield EVERY parked entry, while RustExplorationManager::parked_bounces_flushable_count (angr-03vl4.15) deliberately excludes resident duplicates and unreplayable kinds — a census must equal the post-flush stash population, a broadcast must reach every state that can still execute. Regression pattern: manager_methods_tests.rs::set_{deterministic,max_history}_reaches_parked_{pending_callback,parallel_bounce}_states / pending_api_tests.rs::active_states_map_memory_reaches_parked_{pending_callback,parallel_bounce}_states — assert over several values, or prove non-vacuity by mutating away each arm, so a one-way latch or the default cannot pass. Distinct from invariant-find-state-mut-covers-pending, which is about the single-state API already reaching pending. TEARDOWN DUAL (angr-6cp06.27): the same three-bucket rule applies in reverse to any "replace/discard the whole live-state world" operation, not just broadcasts — manager_methods_snapshot.rs::load_snapshot_bytes cleared both parked buckets, state_lifecycle.rs::_reset_for_stage did not, so a state parked mid-callback (or a wave's undispatched bounce) survived a multi-stage-explore stage transition and leaked stage-1 constraints/history into the next stage's frontier. Teardown differs from broadcast in one way: load_snapshot_bytes swaps in a fresh StashManager so the index goes with it, while _reset_for_stage keeps ours — a keeper must ALSO sm.unindex + sm.remove_root each discarded parked id or stash_of keeps answering for a dead id (angr-ph300.26 in a different bucket). Do NOT call policy.on_state_removed for a parked state: it already left STASH_ACTIVE through policy.select, which notifies. Skip the id being retained — a parked bounce may legitimately duplicate a stash-resident state.
 THIRD AXIS (angr-fs8kb.9): teardown must also sweep manager-level per-stage AGGREGATE bookkeeping that is keyed by nothing — not a stash, not a parked bucket, not even a StateId. constraints.rs::ConstraintTracker::uniqueness_set (a HashSet<u64> of register-tuple hashes, filled by helpers.rs::apply_uniqueness_filter) survived _reset_for_stage, so a legitimate stage-2 state whose hash collided with ANY stage-1 state went to not_unique (or was dropped outright under drop_terminal_states) and vanished from exploration. The three-bucket walk cannot catch this class — all_live_states enumerates states, and this field holds no states. Rule for a new manager field: ask whether its contents are scoped to one run/stage; if yes it belongs in _reset_for_stage (and load_snapshot_bytes) explicitly. The two sibling sets skip_find_predicate_states / skip_avoid_predicate_states are the counter-example that stays: they are keyed by the monotonic StateId, never reused, so a stale entry can only match a dead id. Regression: state_lifecycle_tests.rs::reset_for_stage_clears_uniqueness_seen_set, which asserts behaviourally (a stage-2 state reusing a stage-1 register tuple stays active) as well as by set size — both halves mutation-checked, since a size-only assert would pass on any code path that merely happened to leave the set empty.
invariant-config-mutator-stales-persiste: steady_config_guard is NOT the whole config-invalidation story: it finalizes the live parallel_session, but leaves parallel_pool (the PersistentPool) untouched, and BOTH lazy creation sites (run_loop_wave.rs::run_loop_parallel_wave, run_loop_steady.rs::ensure_steady_session) are guarded on 'if self.parallel_pool.is_none()' with no resize path on PersistentPool. So any config a pool bakes in at creation time goes stale silently the moment a setter changes it — set_parallel_workers(N) was inert for the manager's whole life after the first parallel run (angr-5mnx3.14), which rust_manager.py::_engage_parallel_workers hits on every explore(). Rule for a future setter that feeds pool construction: after the #[steady_guarded] injection, call run_loop.rs::retire_parallel_pool_for_resize (or an analogue) to drop the mismatched pool so the is_none() path rebuilds it; release the GIL around the drop (Python::attach + py.detach, same reasoning as RustExplorationManager::drop) and refuse to drop while a session survived the guard, since joining live workers deadlocks. Keeping the pool is right when the new config means the pool is simply unused (workers<=1 routes to must_run_serial), so the downgrade/restore cycle does not pay a thread-spawn + Z3-context rebuild per explore.
invariant-ctype-mirror-python-not-rust-s: Native ctype procs must mirror angr/procedures/libc/*.py, NOT Rust's std char classifiers — the sets differ, AND must compare the argument at its FULL width, not its low byte. (1) Predicate sets: NativeIsSpace (native/angr/src/procedures/ctype.rs) used Rust's is_ascii_whitespace, which omits \v (0x0b), while Python's isspace and libc accept c==32 || 9<=c<=13 (angr-9ke6b.107). Rust's is_alphanumeric/is_whitespace family is Unicode/Rust-defined, not C-locale defined. When adding or auditing a ctype proc, read the Python SimProcedure's predicate and encode THAT via ranges_predicate/set_predicate; a std one-liner that looks equivalent is the trap. (2) Argument width (angr-6cp06.1): the arg arrives as an arch-word RustBV, and Python's default SimProcedure prototype is all-char*, so its 'c' is arch-word too and 'And(c >= 48, c <= 57)' compares all 64 bits unsigned. Truncating to bits[7:0] made isdigit(304) true natively / false in Python, made case_shift return the truncated byte so tolower(EOF) yielded 255 instead of -1, and made the symbolic path outright UNSOUND (solver satisfies a byte-only predicate for c outside [0,255]). ranges_predicate/set_predicate/arg_in_range now compare at arg.width(), and case_shift returns the argument verbatim on the out-of-range arm. The concrete path derives its answer from the SAME ranges/members table (in_ranges/in_set) as the symbolic disjunction — there is deliberately no separate 'concrete_check' closure to drift. [UPDATE angr-2j9sk] The sibling divergence in strtod.rs/strtol.rs is FIXED and all whitespace classification shares procedures::ctype::is_c_space — see invariant-native-whitespace-single-source.
invariant-dead-code-sweep-siblings: Dead-code removal must sweep for same-named siblings in other structs, not just the one struct the bead names. angr-xvnz removed RustSimState.dirty_registers as a zero-consumer bitset but left VEXInterpreter.dirty_registers (interpreter/mod.rs) — an identical write-only bitset fed by mark_register_dirty from statements.rs's Put/PutI arms — alive for months until angr-0jh0j.27 found it again. Before closing a dead-field/dead-fn removal, grep the whole crate for the bare symbol name (not the qualified path) and remove every copy in the same commit; the second copy is usually in the layer above or below, sharing the concept but not the type. Same discipline as refactor-memory-sweep-rule, applied to code instead of memories.
invariant-dedup-set-ptr: LocalConstraints.dedup_set is a HashSet<usize> of Z3_ast ptrs that tracks every assertion currently asserted on the solver (shared + local z3_assertions). Invariant: 'ptr-in-set => already asserted on the current solver state, AND tracked in either z3_assertions_shared or local.z3_assertions.' Maintained by: lazy-seed on first add_constraint_raw call (one walk of shared+local, in SymContext::seed_and_check_z3_dedup), LocalConstraints::push_assertion on subsequent inserts, dedup_set.clear() + seeded=false on transaction_rollback. When adding new code paths that push to z3_assertions, use LocalConstraints::push_assertion (for a known-new Bool) or SymContext::seed_and_check_z3_dedup / contains_or_insert_ptr (which push on a miss) -- direct .push()/.extend() on the Vec leaves the set stale and breaks the invariant. There is deliberately NO bulk push helper: the one that existed, LocalConstraints::extend_assertions, recorded ptrs but never CONSULTED the set, which is exactly how add_constraints_raw_batch shipped for months re-pushing/re-asserting/double-counting already-asserted constraints and minting spurious ScopeFrames under shared lineage (angr-5mnx3.43, fixed 2026-08-28; the batch now filters through seed_and_check_z3_dedup and extend_assertions is deleted). Safety claim relies on Z3 hash-consing: live AST ptrs are unique among structurally distinct nodes (z3-rs holds refs via Bool::clone preventing GC reuse). PERF COROLLARY (angr-mwbp, was invariant-dedup-seeding-quadratic-cost): the lazy-seed cost (O(N) walk over shared+local z3_assertions on first call) is paid PER-CONTEXT. Branch-heavy benches fork many contexts; if each fork pays the seed cost on its first dedup-checking call, the total work is quadratic in exploration depth -- flareon2015_2 went from 5s to 30s timeout when unconditional seeding was added from assume_*/false. Mitigation: piggy-back dedup checks on whatever seeded the table (typically add_constraint_raw); do NOT trigger seeding from hot paths in fresh contexts. add_constraints_raw_batch DOES seed (measured no regression: flareon2015_2 3.25s vs 3.81s baseline) because it is the same Python-originated SimSolver.add class of traffic as add_constraint_raw, not a per-branch hot path; add_bv_constraint remains un-deduped.

invariant-div-by-zero-total-semantics: Rust engine div-by-zero semantics are TOTAL and the concrete folds must match the symbolic (Z3) arms exactly — verified + regression-covered by angr-g2je6 (commit 12f946f5c). The contract: udiv(x,0)=all-ones, urem(x,0)=srem(x,0)=x, and sdiv(x,0) = -1 for x>=0 but +1 for x<0 (SMT-LIB bvsdiv is asymmetric — this is the trap; the old fold returned all-ones unconditionally). VEXOps::divmod_double_to_single (vex/ops/int_arith.rs) packs the LOW divisor_w bits of those same full-width totals on a zero divisor (quotient low half, remainder high half = the dividend), NOT zero. Concrete folds live in RustBV::{sdiv,udiv,srem,urem}_into (symbolic/value_ops.rs). Two secondary invariants: (1) any concrete signed div/rem fold must use wrapping_div/wrapping_rem — plain / and %% panic on i128::MIN / -1 even in release, and panic=abort SIGABRTs the process (same guard divmod_double_to_single already carried, angr-n0xru); (2) the test pattern that proves alignment is: build the value concretely, then build the SAME expression with a symbolic operand pinned via ctx.add_constraint(pinned.to_z3_ast().eq(z3::ast::BV::from_u64(1,1))) and compare ctx.eval — see test_sdiv_by_zero_concrete_matches_z3 (value_concrete_arm_tests.rs) and divmod_zero_divisor_matches_symbolic (ops/tests_int_arith.rs). Note angr's Python engine instead RAISES ClaripyZeroDivisionError on concrete SDiv-by-zero; PRODUCE_ZERODIV_SUCCESSORS is promoted-to-raise so those states route to Python (angr-op0dn.14.9).
invariant-divmod-generic-helper: Generic divmod_double_to_single (now in native/angr/src/vex/ops/int_arith.rs after the ops.rs split; symbol-anchored) handles all VEX DivMod{U,S}{64to32,128to64} via dividend_w = 2*divisor_w. CONCRETE PATH -- CRITICAL: the concrete signed branch must sign-extend the dividend from its declared width to i128, NOT just 'value as i128' -- for divmod_64_to_32 the dividend's bit 63 IS its sign bit, but treating a u128 with high bits=0 as i128 always gives a positive number. Use sign_extend_low_to_i128(value, width). Same applies to the divisor (sign-extended from divisor_w). Result packing is (quotient | (remainder << divisor_w)) at dividend_w bits. SYMBOLIC PATH (was invariant-divmod-symbolic; both signed+unsigned IROp variants): extend divisor to dividend width using zero_extend for unsigned ops or sign_extend for signed, then udiv/sdiv + urem/srem on the extended pair, finally extract low N/2 bits of each and concat(remainder, quotient). Result format is low = quotient, high = remainder -- concat puts self in high, other in low, so concat(remainder, quotient). Z3's div/mod by zero is total and matches claripy, so no explicit zero guard is needed for the symbolic path.
invariant-doc-example-copies-sweep: A code example that appears in BOTH a docs/*.rst worked example and a Rust module doc (//!) is one logical example with N copies, and a signature change reaches only the copy the author happened to be looking at. Concrete recurrence: angr-c7xno.64 fixed the stale 3-arg scan_for_null(state, addr, MAX_STRLEN) in simprocedures.rst -- and missed a SECOND copy 150 lines lower in the same file plus a third in procedures/macros.rs's module doc; both survived until angr-0jh0j.41/.39 two rounds later. RULE: when a shared helper's signature or dispatch changes, grep the helper/symbol name across docs/**/*.rst AND native/angr/src/**/*.rs doc comments -- not just the one file you are editing, and not just once per file (grep -n, count the hits, fix all of them). The line-citation gate (tools/check_line_citations.py) does NOT catch this class: a wrong argument list carries no line number. Same reasoning as refactor-memory-sweep-rule, applied to doc copies instead of bd memories.
invariant-doc-worked-example-guard-drift: INVARIANT (docs): a fix that adds a *guard* to a function used as a worked example in docs/ must update that example in the same commit. Two independent round-5 audit findings were this exact shape: docs/extending-angr/simprocedures.rst's 'Worked example 3: malloc' lost NativeMalloc's check_max(size, MAX_ALLOC_SIZE)? the moment angr-03vl4.53 added it (the section had been refreshed one commit earlier, for an unrelated reason, so 'recently touched' is no evidence of currency), and docs/extending-angr/rust_vex_ops.rst's BYPASS matrix kept a dead Iop_Perm8x32 opcode after angr-sqfj8.117 remapped the family. Why it is worse than ordinary doc rot: an example is *copied*, so a missing guard propagates the hole the guard closed into every new procedure written from it — stale prose merely misleads. Neither tools/check_line_citations.py nor any other CI gate can see this class (no line number, no symbol rename), so the only defense is the fix author grepping docs/ for the function/opcode name they just changed. Applies to any declare_proc!/register_procs! sample, VEX opcode table, or API snippet.
invariant-eager-concretize-pattern: Eager-concretize pattern in interpreter: when as_u64() fails for a value that must be concrete (PutI/GetI index, exit target, dirty-call args), use ctx.eval(&val) -> Option<u128>, build RustBV::concrete(eval_result, val.width()), construct val.eq(&conc_bv, ctx), then ctx.assume_true(&constraint). This pins the value while preserving constraint history for forks/Python sync. Wrapped as VEXInterpreter::concretize_and_pin (expressions.rs). Used at: GetI/PutI register-array index — since angr-sqfj8.65 both share VEXInterpreter::regarray_offset (expressions.rs), called from eval_geti and the IRStmt::PutI arm in statements.rs (originally pinned separately by angr-eg6j); exit-target concretization (exits.rs); dirty-call args (statements_dirty.rs VEXInterpreter::dirty_arg_values). invariant-enable-nx-gated-on-strict: ENABLE_NX (X-bit non-executable check) is gated on BOTH enforce_permissions (STRICT_PAGE_ACCESS) AND enforce_nx (ENABLE_NX) in SymbolicMemory::check_executable (native/angr/src/memory/mod.rs).
